HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Intimate close three-shot, slight high angle, in a dim county-house room at night. Very old MURYUK, white-haired, gaunt, propped on bolsters under a plain quilt, cradles a NEWBORN swaddled in plain white cotton with a narrow band of Silla-blue #2A5FB8 silk at the edge of the wrap; the baby's tiny fist is closed around the old man's forefinger. His lips are just parted, saying one word, eyes wet and far away. MANMYUNG, young and tired, kneels at his side, her hands still lifted from laying the baby down. SEOHYEON, his grown son, leans in close from the other side, ear turned to his father's mouth, face tight with grief. One low lamp on the floor rakes across the old man's face, the white swaddle and the joined hands; Silla blue #2A5FB8 only in the silk band; deep umber falloff behind. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = muryuk, SECOND face = manmyung, THIRD face = seohyeon. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. KIM MURYUK — Look: Square weathered Gaya face, heavy brows, long pauses in the eyes; grows grey, then white, but never bald under the helm. Dress: Out of battle: plain dark Gaya-cut po with a purple sash; his Gaya helm (rounded iron bowl, wide flared brim, tall red horsehair cone) on his head or under his arm, ALWAYS, even indoors at home (it sits on a stand by the door at night). Now: Very old: white beard, a stick, four blankets, the helm still on. Colour #8B5CF6. MANMYUNG — Look: Young royal Kim noblewoman whose face runs in the family: mostly her granddaughter Gotaso's (oval face, bright almond eyes, small nose, cheerful sly mouth) with a touch of her daughter Munhee's long jaw and arched brows; one eyebrow up, a closed-mouth smirk. Black hair in a high round bun with loose strands at the temples, one gold binyeo with a red bead, small gold hoop earrings. Dress: Short white silk jeogori with deep crimson collar ribbon and cuffs, long deep-crimson chima with a gold-embroidered waistband, a pale celadon-green shawl; good silk she will ruin in the rain. Colour #c98bb9. KIM SEOHYUN — Look: Gentle long face, apologetic eyes, a careful mouth; a softer cousin of young Yushin's face, never the same man. Completely clean-shaven and long-haired when young (loose topknot, long strands past the jaw); a thin moustache and short beard from his forties. Now: Young official in his twenties, CLEAN-SHAVEN, no beard or moustache: steel-blue silk po, white collar, dark sash, jougwan cap over a loose topknot with long loose strands. Colour #3E8EF0. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
